arxiv-2102-12174.title: Codiskcyclic sets of operators on complex topological vector spaces
arxiv-2102-12174.creator: Mohamed Amouch and Otmane Benchiheb
arxiv-2102-12174.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mohamed Amouch and Otmane Benchiheb. Let X X be a complex topological vector space and L ⁡ ( X ) L(X) the set of all continuous linear operators on X . In this paper, we extend the notion of the codiskcyclicity of a single operator T ∈ L ⁡ ( X ) T\in L(X) to a set of operators Γ ⊂ L ⁡ ( X ) . We prove some results for codiskcyclic sets of operators and we establish a codiskcyclicity criterion.

arxiv-2203-09561.title: Adding Flavor to the SMEFT
arxiv-2203-09561.creator: Admir Greljo, Ajdin Palavrić, and Anders Eller Thomsen
arxiv-2203-09561.description: Abstract We study the flavor structure of the lepton and baryon number–conserving dimension-6 operators in the Standard Model effective field theory (SMEFT). Building on the work of Faroughy:2020ina , we define several well-motivated flavor symmetries and symmetry-breaking patterns that serve as competing hypotheses about the ultraviolet (UV) dynamics beyond the SM, not far above the TeV scale.

arxiv-2209-10459.title: Reply to “Comment on Sequential Single-pion Production Explaining the dibaryon d ∗ ​ ( 2380 ) d^{*}(2380) peak”
arxiv-2209-10459.creator: R. Molina, Natsumi Ikeno, Eulogio Oset
arxiv-2209-10459.description: Abstract In a comment to our paper on “Sequential single-pion production explaining the dibaryon d ∗ ​ ( 2380 ) d^{*}(2380) peak” the authors provide arguments that apparently invalidate our claims and present what they call “proofs” of the dibaryon explanation of the n ​ p → π 0 ​ π 0 ​ d np\to\pi^{0}\pi^{0}d fusion reaction.

arxiv-2212-10019.title: When Do Decompositions Help for Machine Reading?
arxiv-2212-10019.creator: Kangda Wei, Dawn Lawrie, Benjamin Van Durme, Yunmo Chen, Orion Weller
arxiv-2212-10019.description: Abstract Answering complex questions often requires multi-step reasoning in order to obtain the final answer. Most research into decompositions of complex questions involves open-domain systems, which have shown success in using these decompositions for improved retrieval. In the machine reading setting, however, work to understand when decompositions are helpful is understudied.

arxiv-2310-07346.title: Preliminary Results of a Scientometric Analysis of the German Information Retrieval Community 2020-2023
arxiv-2310-07346.creator: Philipp Schaer, Svetlana Myshkina, Jüri Keller
arxiv-2310-07346.description: Abstract The German Information Retrieval community is located in two different sub-fields: Information and computer science. There are no current studies that investigate these communities on a scientometric level. Available studies only focus on the information scientific part of the community.

arxiv-2402-02174.title: Influence of the magneto-volume effect on the transient reflectivity of MnSi
arxiv-2402-02174.creator: J. Kalin ∗, S. Sievers, A. Bauer, H. W. Schumacher, H. Füser, C. Pfleiderer, M. Bieler
arxiv-2402-02174.description: Abstract The magneto-volume effect is a well-established yet frequently overlooked phenomenon in magnetic materials that may affect a wide range of physical properties. Our study explores the influence of the magneto-volume effect on the transient reflectivity of MnSi, a well-known chiral magnet with strong magnetoelastic coupling.

arxiv-2407-07125.title: Rapid Parameter Estimation for Merging Massive Black Hole Binaries Using Continuous Normalizing Flows
arxiv-2407-07125.creator: Bo Liang, Minghui Du*, He Wang*, Yuxiang Xu, Chang Liu, Xiaotong Wei, Peng Xu, Li-e Qiang, Ziren Luo
arxiv-2407-07125.description: Abstract Detecting the coalescences of massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) is one of the primary targets for space-based gravitational wave observatories such as LISA, Taiji, and Tianqin. The fast and accurate parameter estimation of merging MBHBs is of great significance for the global fitting of all resolvable sources, as well as the astrophysical interpretation of gravitational wave signals.

arxiv-2509-09919.title: A Markovian Framing of WaveFunctionCollapse for Procedurally Generating Aesthetically Complex Environments
arxiv-2509-09919.creator: Franklin Yiu, Mohan Lu, Nina Li, Kevin Joseph, Tianxu Zhang, Julian Togelius, Timothy Merino, Sam Earle
arxiv-2509-09919.description: Abstract Procedural content generation often requires satisfying both designer-specified objectives and adjacency constraints implicitly imposed by the underlying tile set. To address the challenges of jointly optimizing both constraints and objectives, we reformulate WaveFunctionCollapse (WFC) as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), enabling external optimization algorithms to focus exclusively on objective maximization while leveraging WFC’s propagation mechanism to enforce constraint satisfaction.

arxiv-2511-13872.title: Dynamic state estimation of hybrid systems: Inverters that switch between grid-following and grid-forming control schemes
arxiv-2511-13872.creator: Bukunmi G. Odunlami, Marcos Netto
arxiv-2511-13872.description: Abstract This paper develops a hybrid system modeling framework for inverters that switch between grid-following and grid-forming control schemes. In particular, such inverters are modeled as hybrid automata with guard conditions on voltage and frequency, and reset maps that maintain consistent phase, frequency, and droop references during mode transitions.

Two major transitions in animal evolution–the origins of multicellularity and bilaterality–correlate with major changes in mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) organization. pmc-11415366.title: Intravenous arachnoid granulation hypertrophy in patients with Parkinson disease
pmc-11415366.creator: Melanie Leguizamon, Colin D McKnight, Tristan Ponzo, Jason Elenberger, Jarrod J Eisma, Alexander K Song, Paula Trujillo, Ciaran M Considine, Manus J Donahue, Daniel O Claassen, Kilian Hett
pmc-11415366.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Intravenous arachnoid granulations (AGs) are protrusions of the arachnoid membrane into the venous lumen and function as contributors to the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow circuit. Patients with Parkinson disease (PD) often present with accumulation of alpha synuclein. Previous works have provided evidence for neurofluid circulation dysfunction in neurodegenerative diseases associated with changes in CSF egress, which may have implications regarding AG morphology.

pmc-11436848.title: Exploring the organic nature, morphological plasticity and ecological significance of Aster like nanoparticles
pmc-11436848.creator: Maxime Fuster, Hermine Billard, Jérémie Mathurin, Ariane Deniset-Besseau, David Albertini, Télesphore Sime-Ngando, Jonathan Colombet
pmc-11436848.description: The smallest entities in aquatic ecosystems, i.e., femtoplankton, are certainly the largest reservoir of uncharacterized biodiversity. Among them, the discovery of mysterious Aster like nanoparticles has raised many questions about their nature, origin and ecology. Here, we highlight the original nature of this new model, organic and composed of enriched-calcium carbohydrates, with no detection of nucleic acids or proteins.

pmc-11532436.creator: Jingyu Wang, Ruina Zhao, Yang Liu, Tieying Hu, Xiaolong Li, Long He, Zhaobin Guo, Cheng Chen, Xixiong Shi
pmc-11532436.description: Oula Tibetan sheep meat has rich nutritional value but relatively poor tenderness. Recently, apoptosis of muscle cells has gradually become a research hotspot for improving meat tenderness during postmortem aging. Smac can promote the decrease of IAPs expression in tumor cells, thereby inducing mitochondrial apoptosis.

pmc-11592993.title: Gut Microbiome and Carotid Artery Intima-Media Thickness: A Narrative Review of the Current Scenario
pmc-11592993.creator: Barbara Pala, Giuliano Tocci, Giulia Nardoianni, Emanuele Barbato, Amedeo Amedei, Sonu M M Bhaskar
pmc-11592993.description: Up to the last update, the gut microbiome (GM) had been associated with a different physiologic host process, including those affecting cardiovascular health. The carotid intima-media thickness (IMT) is an indicator of atherosclerosis and cardiovascular risk. The GM influence on atherosclerosis progression has garnered growing attention in recent years but the consensus in subclinical atherosclerosis remains elusive.

pmc-11604696.title: Quantitative analysis of islet prohormone convertase 1/3 expression in human pancreas donors with diabetes
pmc-11604696.creator: Paola S Apaolaza, Yi-Chun Chen, Kavi Grewal, Yannik Lurz, Severin Boulassel, C Bruce Verchere, Teresa Rodriguez-Calvo
pmc-11604696.description: Aims/hypothesisIslet prohormone-processing enzymes convert peptide hormone precursors to mature hormones. Defective beta cell prohormone processing and the release of incompletely processed peptide hormones are observed prior to the onset of diabetes, yet molecular mechanisms underlying impaired prohormone processing during the development of diabetes remains largely unknown.

pmc-12468079.title: Temporal Dynamics of Extracellular Matrix Remodeling in Anthracycline-Induced Cardiotoxicity
pmc-12468079.creator: Fibi Meshrkey, Somaya Y Ibrahim, Rushita A Bagchi, William J Richardson, David J Grieve
pmc-12468079.description: Anthracyclines are widely used chemotherapeutic agents with proven efficacy against a broad range of malignancies, but their clinical utility is limited by a well-documented, dose-dependent cardiotoxicity. While this toxicity has traditionally been attributed to direct cardiomyocyte injury, emerging evidence highlights the pivotal role of cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) in the development and progression of anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity.

pmc-12554022.title: Selection of specific and efficient siRNAs in new cellular model for Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome therapy
pmc-12554022.creator: Volha Dzianisava, Katarzyna Piekarowicz, Magdalena Machowska, Ryszard Rzepecki
pmc-12554022.description: Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome is a fatal genetic disorder caused by a point mutation in the gene encoding the nuclear envelope protein lamin A/C. The most frequent mutation leads to the synthesis of a shorter version of lamin A named progerin, which accumulates under the nuclear membrane, leading to nuclear lamina disorganization and affecting gene expression and signaling.

pmc-13085365.title: Safety and optimal timing of staged nipple-sparing mastectomy following nipple repositioning in ptotic breasts: a systematic review protocol
pmc-13085365.creator: Yousef Tanas, Grace Gasper, Sarya Swed, Aldona J. Spiegel
pmc-13085365.description: BackgroundIn ptotic/macromastic breasts, nipple-sparing mastectomy (NSM) risks ischemic complications. Staging with nipple repositioning (mastopexy or breast reduction) may improve perfusion, but uncertainty remains regarding safety and optimal timing.MethodsPRISMA guidelines will be followed. The database search will be conducted using MEDLINE (PubMed), Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, and ClinicalTrials.
